Aker Lake
lakes.description: Aker Lake (also spelled Ackre) is a 2-acre impoundment of Fish Creek. The history of the dam is not known. Maximum depth is believed to be less than 10 feet. It is stocked annually with sub-catchable and catchable sized Apache trout and arctic grayling. Stocked trout in Aker Lake do not grow rapidly to catchable size due to poor water quality. Because it is a shallow, nutrient-rich lake, water quality problems due to excessive weed growth can cause fish kills in the summer and winter months. Fish Creek is a perennial stream entering the lake. The lake receives inflow from a small watershed with snowmelt, and ground water contributions. The area can receive significant rain during the summer months, however these rains have little influence on lake levels. Aside from the fishery, the lake is primarily a water source for livestock and wildlife as water is not released for downstream irrigation uses. There are no water rights associated with Aker Lake. Due to damage to the fish barrier from the Wallow fire, Fish Creek is no longer an Apache trout recovery stream.

lakes.name: Alamar Park Pond
lakes.description: Alamar pond is a 2.4 acre fishing pond within a 40 acre community park located in the City of Avondale. The park is open for fishing from 6 Am to 10 pm 7 days a week. Swimming, boating, or operating toys in the lake is prohibited.

lakes.name: Alamo Lake
lakes.description:
Alamo Lake is 3,683 acres located on the Bill Williams River below the confluence of the Big Sandy, Santa Maria, and Date Creek tributaries. Fluctuating water levels are common in the reservoir, and water levels can rise up to 7 vertical feet in twenty-four hours. The reservoir was created with the completion of Alamo Dam in 1968. The earthen dam is approximately 39 miles upstream of the Colorado River at Lake Havasu.

Alamo Lake State Park, located on the southwest end of Alamo Lake, provides both primitive and improved camping, and paved boat launches. For park entrance fees visit Alamo State Park. There is a small store in the Park, where you can get ice, snacks, fishing tackle and bait, as well as information on current fishing. A certified scale is located at the store. No fuel is available at Alamo Lake. It is sold at Wenden and nearby Wayside.

There is a fish consumption advisory for black crappie, channel catfish, and largemouth bass in Alamo Lake. See ADEQ for more information.

lakes.name: Alvord Lake
lakes.description: Alvord Lake is a 25 acre lake with a maximum depth of 18 feet. The lake is located within Cesar Chaves Park and can be accessed between 5:30 a.m. and 11:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. Fishing from boat is prohibited. For additional information, please visit Phoenix Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (602) 262-6111.

lakes.name: Apache Lake
lakes.description:
Dubbed by some as the “hidden gem of the Salt River lakes,” Apache Lake is a secluded, 2,656-acre reservoir on the Tonto National Forest. The uncrowded atmosphere is welcoming to boaters, fishing, paddlers, hikers, campers and all outdoor recreation enthusiasts. Surrounded by the Superstition Wilderness, the lake has abundant populations of sport fish.

There is a fish consumption advisory for largemouth bass in Apache Lake. See ADEQ for more information.

lakes.name: Arivaca Lake
lakes.description:
Remote and primitive, Arivaca Lake is located in the rolling grasslands of southern Arizona, near the Mexican border and Buenos Aires National Wildlife Refuge. The Arizona Game and Fish Department owns and operates this remote 80-acre lake. Arivaca Lake is best known for fishing, but it has great canoeing, small sail boating, wildlife viewing and rock climbing opportunities as well. Largemouth bass are highly sought by anglers, while sunfish see a lot of pressure from fly anglers in the spring.

The lake is one of the stops along the historic Ruby Road scenic drive.

There is a fish consumption advisory for largemouth bass in Arivaca Lake. See ADEQ for more information.

lakes.name: Ashurst Lake
lakes.description: Ashurst Lake is a 229-acre reservoir located on Anderson Mesa on the Coconino National Forest. Ashurst Lake features a gravel boat launch, two campgrounds, and pit toilets. The Department manages Ashurst Lake as a trout fishery and regularly stocks rainbow and brown trout. The Department occasionally stocks tiger trout.

lakes.name: Bartlett Lake
lakes.description:
This 2,815-acre reservoir on the Tonto National Forest tends to have extremely consistent fishing opportunities for largemouth bass. Recreational opportunities include good shoreline camping. Common sights can include coyotes, bald eagles, mule deer, and numerous indigenous desert plans. Boat rentals also are available, and Bartlett Flat has primitive boat launch opportunities for small boats.

Water levels fluctuate annually due to water releases by the Salt River Project to meet water demands. To see current levels, check the daily water level report.

There is a fish consumption advisory for channel catfish, flathead catfish, and largemouth bass in Bartlett Lake. See ADEQ for more information.

lakes.name: Bear Canyon Lake
lakes.description:
A beautiful, narrow and canyon-bound lake, Bear Canyon Lake is another in a series of lakes built by Arizona Game and Fish Department to provide fishing opportunities for anglers. Despite being several miles down a dirt road and having few amenities, it draws many visitors. It's a scenic drive to the lake on Forest Road 300 (known locally as the Rim Road or 300 road), which offers several lookout points with spectacular vistas and views from the edge of the Mogollon Rim. A short, but somewhat difficult hike is required to reach the lake.

At an elevation of 7.560 feet, the 60-acre Bear Canyon Lake has no launching facilities since it's a walk-in only lake. Due to its depth (max. depth 50-feet), the lake has no water quality problems. The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks Bear Canyon Lake with 12-inch rainbow trout throughout the spring and summer.

Bear Canyon Lake is a “Pack it in-Pack it out” area with no garbage disposal or services at the lake. Please pack out your trash, including discarded fishing line and other tackle.

lakes.name: Becker Lake
lakes.description:
Built in the 1880s and named for Gustav and Julius Becker, Becker Lake is the oldest reservoir in the White Mountains. Located on the Becker Lake Wildlife Area, this 107-acre lake is managed by the Arizona Game and Fish Department as a trophy trout fishery with catch-and-release regulations. The Arizona Game and Fish Department acquired the lake in 1973, and in January 2002, purchased an additional 291 acres to protect and enhance stream and riparian habitat along the Little Colorado River, collectively forming Becker Lake Wildlife Area.

Located just 2 miles east of Springerville at an elevation of 6,910 feet, Becker Lake offers an escape from summer heat for fishing, hiking, and wildlife viewing. The Arizona Game and Fish Department added two hiking trails, including the one-mile Lakeview Trail loop, which follows the western edge of Becker Lake to an observation platform overlooking the southern, marshy end of the lake. Waterfowl and shorebirds, such as white-faced ibis and killdeer, can easily be seen, especially during migration. Wintering bald eagles can be spotted most years in nearby cottonwood trees.

The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks Becker Lake with rainbow and tiger trout in the spring. Many of these fish survive the winter, reaching a good size the following spring. Becker Lake is open to angling year-round, and typically does not freeze over in the winter months.

lakes.name: Benders Pond
lakes.description: Benders Pond is a new Community Fishing Program (CFP) water in the Town of Gila Bend and is located within Rotary Centennial Park. The pond is roughly one acre in size and is managed under the CFP pond concept.

lakes.name: Big Lake
lakes.description:
Big Lake is considered one of the White Mountain’s best fishing lakes!

When mid-summer fishing doldrums set in at White Mountain lakes and streams, Big Lake continues to produce decent fishing action. As with most trout waters in Arizona, catch rates are best in spring, during late April and May after the winter ice thaws, and gets better later in the summer and into fall until freezing over again in late November.

Situated at 9,000 feet in the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests, Big Lake is located about 30 miles south of Springerville and Eagar via Hwy 260 and Hwy 261, and approximately one hour’s drive east from Pinetop using Highways 260 and 273. Access is restricted in the winter when roads are closed due to snow, generally December to early April. Call the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest Springerville District at (928) 333-6200 for the most up-to-date information, or go to Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest - Big Lake.

lakes.name: Black Canyon Lake
lakes.description:
Located on the Apache-Sitgreaves national forests, Black Canyon Lake was one of many lakes built by the Arizona Game and Fish Department along the Mogollon Rim to provide water recreation opportunities for the public. Despite being heavily affected by the 2002 Rodeo-Chediski Fire, the 78-acre Black Canyon Lake remains a popular and beautiful spot for picnics, camping and fishing. Because of the fire, the entire area around Black Canyon Lake is open for day use only due to the danger of falling trees. A shoreline trail leads from the parking lot to the dam.

The Arizona Game and Fish Department provides current lake conditions, including water levels and web cam views.

Contact the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest Black Mesa District Office at (928) 535-7300 for the most up-to-date information, or visit the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest - Black Canyon Lake website.

lakes.name: Bonsall Park Lake
lakes.description: Bonsall Park Pond is a 2 acre pond with a depth of 10 feet. The pond is located within Bonsall Park and can be accessed between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. For additional information, please contact Glendale Parks and Recreation, or call at (623) 930-2000.

lakes.name: Bunch Reservoir
lakes.description:
Bunch Reservoir is one of a trio of lakes on the Little Colorado River commonly known as the Greer Lakes. These high elevation lakes (~8,200 feet) provide trout fishing opportunities in and around the beautiful alpine town of Greer. Water from Bunch Reservoir is diverted for irrigation during summer, making launching a boat difficult due to low water levels. Ice-fishing at Bunch Reservoir can be decent during some winters.

The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks rainbow trout during the spring and summer. Like its two neighboring reservoirs, Bunch Reservoir gets a few brown trout from the Little Colorado River diversion that refills it in the winter; brown trout are not stocked here.

lakes.name: C.C. Cragin Reservoir (Blue Ridge Reservoir)
lakes.description: C.C. Cragin (Blue Ridge) Reservoir is a 275-acre reservoir located on the Coconino National Forest. Anglers will find shoreline fishing difficult due to steep canyon walls, and are advised to use a boat or other watercraft to effectively navigate and fish the lake. The C.C. Cragin Dam was completed in 1964 by the Phelps Dodge Corporation. In 2005, the C.C. Cragin Project was acquired by the Salt River Project and transferred to the Bureau of Reclamation. In 2018 ownership of the reservoir was transferred to SRP and water from C.C. Cragin is now an important water source for the town of Payson, AZ. As a city water supply the reservoir experiences drastic changes in lake level which can make access difficult for boaters.

lakes.name: Canyon Lake
lakes.description: Towering rock walls and lunker largemouth bass mark a unique Canyon Lake experience. A 950-acre reservoir on the Tonto National Forest, Canyon Lake is surrounded by wildlife viewing opportunities that includes bighorn sheep. A barrier-free fishing dock is located in the Boulder Recreation Site, where paddlers and shore anglers can escape heavy wakes.

lakes.name: Carnero Lake
lakes.description: Carnero Lake is a shallow 65-acre headwater impoundment of Carnero Creek. It has a maximum depth of ten feet. It’s quite weedy, which is problematic for fishing, but is also an indicator of a highly productive lake. The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks rainbow and tiger trout in the spring. This lake is subject to periodic winter kills. Low water and poor water quality can cause summer fish kills. The best time to fish at Carnero is in the spring. Once the weeds begin growing, it’s hard to get a boat or float tube from the shore out to open water, and then it’s difficult to even find much open water.

lakes.name: Cataract Lake
lakes.description: Cataract Lake is a 55 acre Lake located one mile northwest of Williams, AZ. Cataract Lake is open for day-use only with no overnight camping available. The Kaibab National Forest manages the day-use area and boat ramp on the east side of the lake. Cataract Park, managed jointly by the City of Williams and Coconino County, is located on the west side of the lake, and is open for day use as well. Much of the northern shore is private property, with the rest being on Kaibab National Forest lands and county-owned property. The East side gate is closed October to April. The lake usually has unsafe ice cover during the winter months.

lakes.name: Chaparral Park Lake
lakes.description: Chaparral Lake is a 10 acre lake with a maximum depth of 15 feet. The lake is located within Chaparral Park, and can be accessed between sunrise and 10:30 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. A permit must be obtained to drink beer in the park. All other alcoholic beverages are prohibited. For additional information, please visit Scottsdale Community Services, or call at (480) 312-2353.

lakes.name: Chevelon Canyon Lake
lakes.description:
Known for producing large trout, Chevelon Canyon Lake is a deep, canyon-bound lake constructed by the Arizona Game and Fish Department in 1965. Because of its remote location, steep topography and hike-in access, it draws only the most determined and physically fit anglers. Access is difficult, requiring a long, steep hike to the lake. Shoreline fishing is challenging due to steep banks. Chevelon Canyon Lake is best fished using canoes or float tubes carried to the dam and shoreline.

Chevelon Canyon Lake covers 208-acres with an average depth of 35 feet (max. depth 80 feet). This remote lake is a quality fishery known for producing large trout. The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks fingerling rainbow trout in spring and fall. Chevelon Canyon Lake also contains naturally reproducing brown trout that grow to trophy size.

The nearby Chevelon Canyon Campground has six primitive sites and a vault toilet. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring. Chevelon Crossing Campground, on FR 504 near its junction with FR 169, is another primitive campground with five sites and a toilet. Camping is free at both of these campgrounds.

lakes.name: City Reservoir (Buckskinner Park)
lakes.description: City Reservoir is a small, six acre pond located one mile south of Williams, AZ at the end of 6th street. Access to City Reservoir is closed during winter months (December to April). The lake usually has unsafe ice cover during the winter.

lakes.name: Cluff Ranch Pond 3
lakes.description:
The Cluff Ranch Pond 3 is located within the Cluff Ranch Wildlife Area at the base of the Pinaleno Mountains near the towns of Pima and Safford. The Arizona Game and Fish Department owns and manages Cluff Ranch Wildlife Area for wildlife recreation, including fishing, upland small game hunting (doves, quail, rabbits), archery deer and javelina hunting and wildlife watching.

Pond 3 is open for fishing.

lakes.name: Copper Sky Lake
lakes.description: Copper Sky Lake is a 5 acre lake with a maximum depth of 13 feet. The lake is located within Copper Sky Recreation Complex, and can be accessed between sunrise and 11:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. For additional information, please visit City of Maricopa Community Services Department, or call at (520) 316-6960.

lakes.name: Cortez Park Lake
lakes.description: Cortez Lake is a 3 acre lake with a maximum depth of 14 feet. The lake is located within Cortez Park, and can be accessed between 5:30 a.m. and 11:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. For more information, please visit Phoenix Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (602) 262-6575.

lakes.name: Council Avenue Pond
lakes.description: Council Avenue Pond is a 1 acre pond with a maximum depth of 8 feet. The pond is located within Council Avenue Park, and is open between 5:00 a.m. and 11:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. Leashed dogs are permitted in the park. All vehicles are prohibited from entering the park. Wheeled vehicles are prohibited from the walkway during the hours of 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. and 9:00 p.m. For additional information, please visit Somerton Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (928) 722-7384.

lakes.name: Cowpuncher Pond
lakes.description: Cowpuncher Pond is a new Community Fish Program (CFP)water in the Town of Gila Eagar and is located within Ramsey Park. The pond is roughly two acres in size and is managed under the CFP pond concept for regulations.

lakes.name: Crescent Lake
lakes.description:
It should be noted that the Department does not currently stock this lake due to low water levels. Please check the stocking schedule or call the Pinetop Regional Office prior to fishing Crescent Lake. When conditions are right, usually in June through early August, the fishing action at Crescent Lake can rival that of its mighty neighbor to the south, Big Lake. A former state record brook trout was caught at Crescent Lake.
 
 At 100-acres, Crescent Lake has an average depth of 10 feet. It’s a highly productive lake, which allows trout to gain size quickly. However, the lake is shallow, which encourages weed growth and algae blooms, and makes it subject to late summer and winter fish kills. To manage the problem of winter kills, the Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks the lake with large numbers of rainbow and brook trout each spring. Projects are in progress to help alleviate summer and winter fish kills.
 
 Crescent Lake is located approximately 2 miles north of Big Lake, at the junction of State Highways 261 and 273. It is less than 30 miles southwest of Springerville and Eager by paved road, or less than an hour’s drive from Pinetop using Highways 260 and 273. The lake is normally open from April to November. Weather can change the dates the lake is accessible. Call the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest Springerville District at (928) 333-6200 for the most up-to-date information.

lakes.name: Crystal Gardens Wetlands
lakes.description: Crystal Gardens Wetlands is a City of Avondale Wetland project designed to treat the City's Salt River Project and Central Arizona Project water allocations. The project was designed to be an amenity to the community as well as a source of drinking water. City staff raise approximately 6,000 fish annual and relase them into the wetlands.

lakes.name: Dankworth Pond
lakes.description: Dankworth Pond is located in Dankworth Pond State Park, 8 miles (13 km) south of Safford in southeastern Arizona. The pond is fed by a live artesian spring which is very warm to the touch (~90°). At one time there were actually several ponds used for commercial catfish farming by the Dankworth family. The property opened as a part of Roper State Park in 1982. The pond is now home to rainbow trout, largemouth bass, channel catfish, redear and bluegill sunfish. In addition to fish calling the pond home, waterfowl, migratory birds, and a lot of other wildlife are also found in the area.

lakes.name: Dave White Regional Park Pond
lakes.description: Dave White Pond is a 1 acre pond with a maximum depth of 12 feet. The pond is located within Dave White Regional Park, and can be accessed between sunrise and 11:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. For additional information, please visit City of Casa Grande Community Services Department, or call at (520) 421-8677.

lakes.name: Dead Horse State Park Lagoons
lakes.description:
Ease of walking while fishing is an advantage when enjoying this series of three lagoons in Dead Horse State Park. Surrounded by open fields and walking paths, fishing at Dead Horse is an ideal option for kids or those with physical challenges.

The lagoons (Upper, Middle, and Lower) are located in Dead Horse Ranch State Park in central Arizona, along the Verde River and north of the town of Cottonwood. A former working ranch site, it is now a popular recreation park with camping, fishing, cabins, hiking, paddling, and bird watching. The lagoons provide excellent fishing opportunities for beginners, families, and more advanced anglers. Fly-fishing the Verde River and lagoons is becoming increasingly popular. The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks both the Verde River and two of the three lagoons with rainbow trout throughout the winter months, and channel catfish during warmer weather.

Canoeing and kayaking are popular activities in the lower (east and middle) lagoons, which is limited to non-motorized watercraft (oars only, no sails). The east lagoon has a launch ramp and dock; gas and electric motors must be removed before launching.

lakes.name: Desert Breeze Lake
lakes.description: Desert Breeze Lake is a 4 acre lake with a maximum depth of 12 feet. The lake is located within Desert Breeze Park, and can be accessed between 6:00 a.m. and 10:30 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. For additional information, please visit Chandler Community Services Department, or call at (480) 782-2727.

lakes.name: Desert West Lake
lakes.description: Desert West Lake is a 5 acre lake with a maximum depth of 15 feet. The lake is located within the Desert West Park and Sports Complex, and can be accessed between 5:30 a.m. and 11:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. For additional information, please visit Phoenix Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (602) 262-6576.

lakes.name: Discovery District Park
lakes.description: Discovery Ponds are comprised of an upper and lower pond with a maximum depth of 12 feet. The upper pond is 1 acre, and the lower pond is 2 acres. The ponds are located within Discovery Park, and can be accessed between 5:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. For additional information, please visit Gilbert Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (480) 503-6200.

lakes.name: Dogtown Reservoir
lakes.description: Dogtown Lake got its name from the extensive prairie dog "towns" that once covered open areas near the lake. Located just six miles southeast of Williams, AZ on the Kaibab National Forest, Dogtown Lake offers abundant shoreline fishing under Ponderosa Pines. The Kaibab National Forest operates Dogtown Lake Campground, which is generally open  from early April to the end of September. During the rest of the year, Dogtown Lake is open for day use only. Access varies depending on weather, snowfall, and road conditions. The lake usually has unsafe ice cover during the winter.

lakes.name: Eldorado Park Lake
lakes.description:
*The lake is currently under construction.*
Eldorado Pond is a 3.5 acre pond with a maximum depth of 10 feet. The lake is located within Eldorado Park, and can be accessed between sunrise and 10:30 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. Feeding wildlife (e.g. ducks, geese, pigeons) is unlawful. For additional information, please visit Eldorado Park and Community Center, or call at (480) 312-2483.

lakes.name: Elk Tank
lakes.description: Elk Tank is located approximately eighteen miles southeast of Williams, AZ on the Kaibab National Forest. Visitors access is walk in only (~0.25 mi) from the parking area on Forest Road 11. During winter months, the road to Elk Tank may be closed depending on snowfall.

lakes.name: Encanto Park Lake
lakes.description: Encanto Lake is a 7.5 acre lake with a maximum depth of 10 feet. The lake is located within Encanto Park, and can be accessed between 5:30 a.m. and 11:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. Fishing is prohibited from the golf course as posted. For additional information, please visit Phoenix Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (602) 261-8991.

lakes.name: Evelyn Hallman Pond
lakes.description: Evelyn Hallman Pond is a 3 acre pond with a maximum depth of 7 feet. The pond is located within Evelyn Hallman Park, and can be accessed between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. A permit is required to drink beer in the park, however all other alcoholic beverages are prohibited. For additional information, please visit Tempe Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (480) 350-5200.

lakes.name: Fain Lake
lakes.description: One of the more recent additions to the Arizona Game and Fish Department's Community Fishing Program, Fain Lake is stocked to provide angling opportunities to valid Arizona fishing license holders. The Fains, one of the area’s original frontier families, donated a 100-acre parcel of land to the citizens of Prescott Valley, opening as Fain Park in 1997. The Town of Prescott Valley encourages recreational activities, such as fishing, picnicking, hiking, and even gold panning.

lakes.name: Festival Fields Pond
lakes.description: Festival Fields pond is a 2.5 acre pond within the Festival Fields park of Avondale. This water follows the pond daily bag limits and is open from 6 am to 11 pm. Swimming, wading, boating, glass containers are prohibited. for additional information please visit ; https://www.avondaleaz.gov/government/departments/parks-recreation/parks

lakes.name: Fool Hollow Lake
lakes.description:
Fool Hollow was named for a hapless settler who attempted to farm the rocky canyon in the 1880s. With a variety of fish species, Fool Hollow Lake offers something for everyone, from first-time anglers to seasoned veterans. Even though the lake has first-rate visitor amenities and is minutes from Show Low, its craggy banks and beautiful vistas give visitors a feeling of seclusion.

The Arizona Game and Fish Department constructed the lake in 1957 to provide water-oriented outdoor recreation. Located at an elevation of 6,250 feet, this 150-acre lake is located within the Fool Hollow Recreation Area, and is cooperatively managed by the Arizona Game and Fish Department, the City of Show Low, Arizona State Parks, and the U.S. Forest Service.

The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks the lake with rainbow trout throughout the spring and summer.

lakes.name: Fortuna Lake
lakes.description: Fortuna Lake is a 9 acre lake, which is open 24 hours a day. The lake is surrounded by mature cottonwood and willow trees, and there are groves of mixed mesquite and tamarisk nearby. Maintained gravel roads provide access to the lake. Camping on premises is not allowed. There are no facilities on site. For additional information, please contact the Arizona Game and Fish Department Yuma Regional Office at (928) 342-0091, or the Bureau of Land Management Yuma Field Office at (928) 317-3200.

lakes.name: Frances Short Pond
lakes.description: Located in Flagstaff, AZ, Frances Short Pond is an impoundment of the Rio de Flag. The pond is named after late educator and city councilperson Frances Short. However, it is also referred to as the “duck pond” by local residents due to the presence of resident ducks that call the pond home. Frances Short Pond is very popular wildlife viewing spot due to ample habitat for water-loving birds. The pond is easily accessible from downtown Flagstaff, and visitors enjoy scenic views of the San Francisco Peaks. Frances Short Pond was restored in 2005 with funding from the Arizona Game and Fish Department to provide an angling opportunity. The pond was renovated again in 2023 following the Pipeline Fire.

lakes.name: Freestone Park
lakes.description: Freestone Lake is a 2 acre lake with a maximum depth of 10 feet. The lake is located within Freestone Park, and can be accessed between 5:30 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. For additional information, please visit Gilbert Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (480) 503-6200.

lakes.name: Friendship Park Pond
lakes.description: Friendship Pond is a 1 acre pond with a maximum depth of 12 feet. The pond is located within Friendship Park, and can be accessed between 6:00 a.m. and 11:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. For additional information, please visit Avondale Parks, Recreation and Libraries, or call at (523) 333-2400.

lakes.name: Frontier Family Park
lakes.description: Frontier Lake is a 5 acre lake within the larger Frontier park complex. Access is permitted from 5:30 am to 10 pm. This lake is not part of the community fishing program.

lakes.name: Frye Mesa Reservoir
lakes.description: Frye Mesa Reservoir is one of few places in Arizona to catch the rare Gila trout, a native species found only in Arizona and New Mexico. The small 4-acre reservoir is located 15 miles south of Safford at the base of Mt. Graham.

lakes.name: Gilbert Regional Park Pond
lakes.description: Gilbert Regional Pond is a 8 acre lake with a maximum depth of 10 feet. The lake is located within Gilbert Regional Park and can be accessed between 5:30 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. For additional information, please visit Gilbert Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (480) 503-6200

lakes.name: Graham County Fair Grounds
lakes.description: Graham County Fair Grounds Pond has two small ponds and the upper pond is 2.5 acres. The ponds are located in Safford and are open Monday to Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

lakes.name: Granite Basin Lake
lakes.description:
Nestled among pines and boulders of Prescott's iconic Granite Mountain, the 5-acre Granite Basin Lake and surrounding area offers plentiful year-round recreation activities, including fishing, non-motorized boating including paddle sports, hiking, backpacking, horse riding, rock climbing, camping, and picnicking.

Granite Basin Lake is not actively stocked by the Arizona Game and Fish Department. Patient anglers may catch bluegill, largemouth bass and catfish. Non-motorized boats may access the lake via a small boat ramp. Visit the Prescott National Forest Granite Basin Lake website for more information, including day use fees. Heavy rain and snow can close access. For the most up-to-date information, contact the Bradshaw Ranger Station at (928) 443-8000.

lakes.name: Granite Dells Lake
lakes.description: Granite Dells Lake is a new pond in Payson, Arizona. The pond has mutliple other ammenities and outdoor activities in the park. The park is currently under construction.

lakes.name: Green Valley Park Lakes
lakes.description: The award-winning Green Valley Park in the town of Payson provides family-friendly fishing for anglers of all ages and abilities. A partnership between the Arizona Game and Fish Department Community Fishing Program and Payson's Parks and Recreation Department intensively stocks and manages the park's lakes for fishing recreation.

lakes.name: Greenfield Park Pond
lakes.description:
Located in the city of Mesa, the 2.5-acre Greenfield Park Pond is stocked by the Arizona Game and Fish Department as part of its Community Fishing Program. The park is open from sunrise to 10pm daily.

For more information visit the city of Mesa's Greenfield Park website.

lakes.name: Heroes Regional Park Pond
lakes.description: Heroes Regional Park Lake is 4 acres in size with a maximum depth of 13 feet.

lakes.name: Horseshoe Reservoir
lakes.description:
Horseshoe Lake is ideal for anglers looking for a quiet place to fish. The 2,722 acre reservoir is one of the most remote lakes in the area. Water levels fluctuate and can be low when the Salt River Project releases water for irrigation and domestic uses.

Additionally, the Salt River Project annually draws down the water level to provide riparian habitat for the native southwest willow flycatcher and to minimize the reproduction and recruitment of non-native fish species in the reservoir. Check the daily water level report.

Bald eagle closures - a portion of the lake is closed from December 1st to June 30th. Contact the Arizona Game and Fish Department at (623) 236-7506 with any questions.

lakes.name: Horsethief Basin Lake
lakes.description: Horsethief Basin Lake was constructed in 1936 by the City of Phoenix to provide water resources to Horsethief Basin Recreation Area.  The lake is 5 surface acres when full. The U.S. Forest Service (USFS) has since assumed management responsibility for the lake and surrounding area.  The lake is currently maintained for recreational opportunities, including sport fishing.

lakes.name: Huffer Tank
lakes.description: Huffer Tank is a small 0.4 acre pond located North of the community of Strawberry, AZ at mile marker 282 on Highway 87 within the West Clear Creek watershed. Rainbow Trout are stocked in the spring and early summer.

lakes.name: J.D. Dam
lakes.description: J.D. Dam is located seven miles south of Whitehorse Lake on the Kaibab National Forest. Facilities are limited to a gravel parking area and primitive restroom. If anglers choose to camp nearby, campsites must be located a 1/4 mile radius away from J.D. Dam. There area has many wildlife watching opportunities including the Sycamore Point viewpoint. Access to J.D. Dam may be closed during the winter months due to heavy snow and ice cover.

lakes.name: Kaibab Lake
lakes.description: Kaibab Lake is a 45 acre lake located on the Kaibab National Forest. Kaibab Lake is popular spot for fishing, picnicking, and camping. With Grand Canyon National Park just 60 miles north and several other cultural and historic sites nearby, the location is a popular location. Access to Kaibab Lake is by a paved road that intersects with Highway 64 about one mile north of the I-40 junction. The lake is open to the public for day use year round, but is frequently inaccessible during the winter due to snow blocking the road to the lake and ice cover on the lake. Amenities at the lake feature Kaibab National Forest campgrounds that are open seasonally from May 1 to the end of September, pit toilets, amphitheater, concrete boat launch, day use area with parking for passenger cars and vehicles with boat trailers, and fishing dock.

lakes.name: Kennedy Lake
lakes.description: Kennedy Lake is a 10-acre lake located in Tucson's John F. Kennedy Park, located near the intersection of Mission Road and Ajo Way in southwest Tucson. The City of Tucson partners with the Arizona Game and Fish Department Community Fishing Program to stock fish into Kennedy Lake several times per year. For additional information, please visit Tucson Parks and Recreation, or call at (520) 791-4873.

lakes.name: Kinnikinick Lake
lakes.description: Kinnikinick Lake is a 126-acre lake located on Anderson Mesa in the Coconino National Forest. Wildlife watching opportunities include elk, deer, pronghorn antelope, waterfowl, bald eagles, and osprey.

lakes.name: Kiwanis Park Lake
lakes.description: Kiwanis Lake is a 13 acre lake with a maximum depth of 8 feet. The lake is located within Kiwanis Park, and can be accessed between 6:00 a.m. to midnight. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. An alcoholic beverage permit is required for beer; all other alcoholic beverages are prohibited. For additional information, please visit Tempe Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (480) 350-5200.

lakes.name: Knoll Lake
lakes.description: Knoll Lake a 77 acre lake located on top of the Mogollon Rim on the Coconino National Forest. Access to the lake is by the FR 300 or Rim Road, FR 295, and FR 295E. Knoll Lake is a high elevation clear water reservoir making it a popular summer recreation spot for anglers and boaters. The lake features a campground open from May to the end of September, concrete boat launch, and pit toilets.

lakes.name: Lake Havasu
lakes.description:
In 2014, Bassmaster Magazine ranked Lake Havasu as one of the top 20 bass lakes in the United States! Created by the completion of Parker Dam in 1938, Lake Havasu is a 19,300-acre impoundment along the Arizona-California border on the Colorado River. The lake gets its name from the Mojave word for blue-green water. Twenty-five miles long with over 60 miles of shoreline, Lake Havasu attracts over 750,000 visitors annually. Popular with anglers and recreational boaters, this reservoir is one of the best fishing lakes in Arizona, if not the entire southwestern United States. Bass fishing tournaments attract both pro and amateur anglers.

Fishing is popular year-round with all ages. Anglers catch largemouth, smallmouth and striped bass, bluegill, redear sunfish, channel catfish and flathead catfish. Bass over 5 lbs. and 20+ lb. carp aren't uncommon. World record-setting redear sunfish have been caught at Lake Havasu a couple of times, first in 2011, then in 2014, and again in 2021 with a 6 lb 4 oz fish. In addition to redear, current Colorado River and State Record fish caught at Lake Havasu include smallmouth bass (6 lb 4.48 oz, 21 in.), carp (42 lb., 43 in.), black crappie (2 lb. 12 oz., 16 in.), and green sunfish (1 lb. 5.28 oz. 11.5 in.). Additionally, the Department has participated in the Lake Havasu Fisheries Improvement Program since 1993 by installing fish habitat into the lake (see AGFD Reservior Fish Habitat Locations). This habitat can provide cover and congregate fish, creating target areas for anglers and improving angler catch rates.

lakes.name: Lake Mary, Lower
lakes.description: Lower Lake Mary is an impoundment of Walnut Canyon in the Little Colorado River Watershed located on the Coconino National Forest and located approximately five miles southeast of the City of Flagstaff, AZ. Construction of the Lower Lake Mary Dam was completed by an early Flagstaff resident family the Riordans’ in 1904 who constructed a pipeline providing water to the town of Flagstaff. Lower Lake Mary has a maximum capacity of 750 surface acres and a maximum depth of 21 feet. On average Lower Lake Mary is 500 surface acres with an average depth of 12 feet. The lake receives water primarily from outflow from Upper Lake Mary when it is full enough to spill. The lake is popular among anglers for growing tremendous trout when the lake fills and holds water for at least two years. However, given the ephemeral nature of the lake and the fact that the lake bed sits on a fault line the water level of Lower Lake Mary fluctuates greatly depending on precipitation and runoff.

lakes.name: Lake Mary, Upper
lakes.description: Upper Lake Mary is located off Lake Mary Road (FH3) just south of Flagstaff, AZ. On average the lake is ~ 450 surface acres, but can swell to close to 900 surface acres when full. Upper Lake Mary attracts power boaters and water skiers because there are no motor restrictions, sail boats due to frequent windy day, and paddle sports due to the proximity to Flagstaff and NAU. Anglers enjoy Upper Lake Mary due to its diverse fish community and the potential to catch a unique or large fish. Upper Lake Mary Boat Launch and Picnic Area offers boat launch and picnic facilities. Upper Lake Mary Narrows Boat Launch and Picnic Area provides excellent access facilities for physically challenged anglers by means of paved lakeshore ramps.

lakes.name: Lake Mead
lakes.description:
The completion of the Hoover Dam in 1935 created Lake Mead, the largest man-made lake in North America. Located just 24 miles from Las Vegas in the Lake Mead National Recreation Area, the reservoir provides water to the states of Arizona, California, and Nevada. Lake Mead has three major basins accessed from various points in Arizona and Nevada, as well as the extensive Overton Arm.

The U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service stocked the first sport fish into Lake Mead in the 1930s, and in the 1950s state wildlife agencies added forage fish (shad), resulting in a flourishing bass fishery. Read more about the history of sport fish in Lake Mead and Lake Mohave, courtesy of the National Park Service.

Check current launch and ramp conditions.

lakes.name: Lake Mohave
lakes.description:
Located in the Lake Mead National Recreation Area, Lake Mohave was created in 1951 following the completion of Davis Dam near Bullhead City, AZ. Named for the Mohave Indians who previously lived in the area along the Colorado River, Lake Mohave offers excellent shoreline camping opportunities. Stretching 67 miles, Lake Mohave's cool, crystal clear waters and secluded coves offers anglers, boaters and scuba divers plenty of opportunities to explore and enjoy a relatively crowd-free experience.

Striped bass are the most sought-after sport fish species in Lake Mohave. The lake also provides critical habitat for two endangered species, razorback sucker and bonytail chub. Once abundant throughout the Colorado River basin, razorback sucker numbers have dropped to less than 5,000; Lake Mohave now contains the largest population of this native species. Bonytail chub exist in very low numbers.

For more information on Lake Mohave, visit National Park Service - Lake Mohave.

Check current launch and ramp conditions.

lakes.name: Lake Pleasant
lakes.description:
Located in the Northwest Valley, Lake Pleasant Regional Park offers boating, fishing, swimming, hiking, picnicking, and wildlife viewing. Lake water levels can fluctuate throughout the year, typically reaching its highest level in the spring (March and April) and its lowest in the fall (October and November). Lake Pleasant was first formed in 1927 with the building of Wadell Dam, which at the time was the largest agricultural dam in the world. The Bureau of Reclamation raised the height of the dam in 1993, increasing the surface area of the lake to 10,000 acres.

Lake Pleasant is known throughout the western states for its excellent scuba diving. With depths approaching 260 ft. when the reservoir is full, rock walls, canyons, and underwater structures, like the old Waddell Dam, welcome underwater explorers.

Bald eagle closures - no vehicle, watercraft, or foot entry is allowed into the Lower Agua Fria River Arm from December 15th to June 15th. Contact Maricopa County Parks and Recreation at (928) 501-1710 with any questions.

There is a fish consumption advisory for largemouth bass and striped bass in Lake Pleasant. See ADEQ for more information.

lakes.name: Lake Powell
lakes.description:
Special Use Stamps (trout stamp, two-pole stamp, Colorado River Stamp- California, Colorado River stamp - Nevada, and Utah Lake Powell Reciprocal License) are no longer required or available. A valid Arizona Fishing license or combination hunt/fish license is all that is required to fish Lake Powell.

Lake Powell is a Colorado River impoundment formed when the newly constructed Glen Canyon Dam was closed in 1963. Water continued to back up behind the dam continually until 1980, when the lake reached full pool and became the second largest reservoir in the United States. Located within the 1.25 million acre Glen Canyon National Recreational Area (AZ), Lake Powell is a major vacation spot and world-class destination for fishing, attracting over three million visitors annually.

Lake Powell, separated from its downstream sister Lake Mead by the Grand Canyon National Park, has some of the best striped bass fishing in the United States. Despite its popularity, anglers come to the 186-mile long Lake Powell to escape the crowds. It's sheer vastness offers anglers and boaters alike numerous opportunities for solitude in side coves, while its remoteness offers unparalleled stargazing. Anglers enjoy an unlimited bag on striped bass, and some of the best smallmouth bass fishing in the western United States.

lakes.name: Lakeside
lakes.description: Lakeside Lake is located within the City of Tucson's Chuck Ford Lakeside Park, and is open 6:00am-10:30pm daily. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. No live baitfish allowed. For additional information, please visit Tucson Parks and Recreation, or call at (520) 791-4873.

lakes.name: Lee Valley Lake
lakes.description:
At 9,418 feet, Lee Valley Lake is Arizona’s highest elevation reservoir.

Loved by fly fishermen for its breathtaking setting, Lee Valley Lake sparkles below the flanks of Mount Baldy. A beautiful lake year-round, Lee Valley is especially glorious in the fall when aspens turn golden and elk bugle, while fish rise at dawn and dusk. On July 10, 1995, an angler at Lee Valley Lake caught the current state record for Arctic grayling at 1 pound, 9.76 ounces and 14.65 inches.

Lee Valley Lake anglers find themselves at the heart of three Apache trout recovery streams. The Apache trout is Arizona’s official state fish. Located on an Apache trout recovery stream, the 35-acre Lee Valley Lake has an average depth of 9.5 feet (max. depth 20 feet). Lee Valley Creek naturally flows into the East Fork of the Little Colorado River, while the spillway directs overflow to the West Fork of the Little Colorado River. Both streams are also designated for Apache trout recovery. The Arizona Game and Fish Department owns water rights in the lake, and maintains water levels at a stable level.

The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks 8-12 inch Apache trout several times a year, and periodically Arctic grayling (when available). Some of these fish overwinter, reaching a good size the following spring.

lakes.name: Long Lake
lakes.description: Long Lake is located on the Coconino National Forest. Long Lake is part of an interconnected series of impoundments (Soldiers Lake, Soldiers Annex Lake, Tremaine Lake, and Hay Lake) used for hay production and to provide water for livestock. Long Lake is the only actively managed impoundment of the complex and is occasionally stocked with rainbow trout when it fills. Access to the lake is by Lake Mary road (FH3) or highway 87, FR 211, and FR 82. Amenities at the lake include to concrete boat launches and pit toilets at either end of the lake. Only high clearance vehicles are recommended to access the complex of lakes.

lakes.name: Long Tom Tank
lakes.description: Long Tom Tank is a small, 3-acre pond located just outside the community of Forest Lakes. The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks Long Tom Tank with rainbow trout in the spring each year. Anglers might also catch illegally introduced bass and sunfish. Since the tank is spring-fed, water levels stay fairly constant throughout the year. A dirt parking lot is located near the lake; however, no other amenities exist.

lakes.name: Lower Goldwater Lake
lakes.description: Nestled in tall pines, beautiful Lower Goldwater Lake is just four miles from downtown Prescott in Goldwater Park. Lower Goldwater Lake is a new part of the Goldwater Lake Park. This portion of the park was just opened to the public in 2022.

lakes.name: Luna Lake
lakes.description:
Luna Lake is the last chance to fish in eastern Arizona before the New Mexico state line.

Large, scenic, with lots of visitor amenities and close to the town of Alpine, Luna Lake offers good spring, early summer and fall fishing for locals and visitors alike.

Luna Lake is the jewel of Luna Lake Wildlife Area, which encompasses the upper end of the lake. Managed by the Arizona Game and Fish Department, Luna Lake Wildlife Area is a great place to observe waterfowl. The wildlife area is closed to public entry annually from April 1 through July 31. The Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest Luna Lake Recreational Area is open year round, with potential for ice-fishing during the winter. Every year, the Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks this 154-acre lake with rainbow and cutthroat trout and native, gila trout, when avaiable, which grow rapidly to a catchable size due to the high productivity of the lake. In October of 1976, an angler at Luna Lake caught the current state record for cutthroat trout at 6 pounds, 5 ounces and 22.3 inches. The high productivity of Luna Lake encourages weed growth and algae blooms, causing late summer and winter fish kills. Projects are in progress to help alleviate these seasonal fish kills.

lakes.name: Lyman Reservoir
lakes.description:
With the largest lake in the region and no boat motor restrictions, Lyman Lake State Park attracts anglers, as well as campers and water skiers, year-round. Located near St. John's, this 1,500-acre lake has an average depth of 22 feet (max. depth 57 feet) when full. Water levels fluctuate since Lyman Lake is part of the local irrigation district, and the lake can experience considerable drawdowns depending on the amount of water being diverted for irrigation.

Arizona State Parks maintains year-round visitor amenities, including a boat ramp, fish-cleaning station, picnic tables, shade ramadas, handicap-accessible restrooms, showers, drinking water and a dump station. Camp sites, with and without hookups, are available for a fee, along with cabins and yurts. A well-stocked convenience store, which sells bait, tackle, ice and firewood, is open from early April until the end of September. In the summer, there are interpretive tours of nearby petroglyphs.

lakes.name: Lynx Lake
lakes.description:
Located in the Lynx Lake Recreation Area just minutes from downtown Prescott, Lynx Lake is one of the most popular recreation areas in central Arizona. Families come here to camp and fish this 55-acre lake, which was built in 1963 by the Arizona Game and Fish Department to meet a growing demand for fishing. The Prescott National Forest improved and expanded camping facilities to accomodate a growing number of campers.

Pine trees and a hiking trail hug the shoreline, although the trail on the east side of the lake is closed December to June of each year to accomodate nesting bald eagles. Additional activities include boating (electric motors only), mountain biking, horseback riding, archaeological sites, and bird watching.

lakes.name: Mansel Carter Oasis Park Lake
lakes.description:
The town of Queen Creek opened Mansel Carter Oasis Park in September 2018. In addition to a 5-acre fishing lake stocked by the Arizona Game and Fish Department, the new family-focused park features play areas, a pirate-themed splash pad, ballfields, exercise course, and a wheel-friendly skate plaza.

The lake at Mansel Carter was designed to be water-efficient. Instead of using precious potable (drinking water), it is filled instead with recovered water, which is then used to water the park's landscaping and turf. To learn more, including how this is saving the town money, please visit Queen Creek's Lake at Masel Carter Oasis Park website.

lakes.name: Marshall Lake
lakes.description: Marshall Lake is a 150-acre wetland that sits on Anderson Mesa within the Coconino National Forest and is primarily habitat for waterfowl. However, during wet cycles when the wetland fills it supports a trout fishery.

lakes.name: Martinez Lake
lakes.description: Martinez Lake is a backwater of the Imperial Division of the Colorado River that is approximately 450 acres. It is accesible from the river and multiple boat launches including Meers Point, Fisher's Landing, and Martinez Lake Marina.

lakes.name: McQueen Park
lakes.description: McQueen Pond is a 2 acre pond with a maximum depth of 10 feet. The pond is located within McQueen Park, and can be accessed between 5:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. For additional information, please visit McQueen Park Activity Center and District Park, or call at (480) 503-6294.

lakes.name: Middle Tank
lakes.description: Middle Tank is a small, three acre stock tank located 18 miles southeast of Williams, AZ, on the Kaibab National Forest. Anglers access the tank by walking in from a small parking area off of Forest Road 11. During winter months the road may be closed due to snow

lakes.name: Mingus Lake
lakes.description: Small and scenic, Mingus Lake is located high in the cool pines of Mingus Mountain. The Prescott National Forest keeps the gate to the parking lot open from May 1 to October 31. Anglers can hike into the lake during other months. Close to Prescott Valley, Jerome and Cottonwood, Mingus Lake is a great spot for fishing and picnicking and has a picnic table, shelter and a vault toilet. No drinking water is available at the site so be sure to bring your own.

lakes.name: Mittry Lake
lakes.description: Mittry Lake is 180 acres and located in the Mittry Lake Wildlife Area on Bureau of Land Management (BLM) lands. A popular local fishing destination, Mittry Lake provides opportunities for both shore and boat angling. Popular sport fish include largemouth bass, sunfish, and catfish.

lakes.name: Nelson Reservoir
lakes.description:
Anyone traveling from Springerville to Alpine has driven by Nelson Reservoir. A long and narrow lake, it follows the Nutrioso Creek Valley for nearly a mile. Fish that remain in Nelson Reservoir after summer stockings can grow to good size, making it a popular fishing site with local anglers. This lake has been known to produce trophy sized black crappie.
 
Nelson Reservoir is subject to algae blooms and excessive weed growth as summer progresses. The lake contains native bluehead suckers and illegally introduced black crappie and green sunfish. The lake sometimes freezes for short periods during the winter, but is typically open to fishing year-round.

lakes.name: Pacana Park
lakes.description: Pacana Pond is a 2 acre pond with a maximum depth of 11 feet. The pond is located within Pacana Park, and can be accessed between sunrise and 11:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. For additional information, please visit City of Maricopa Community Services Department, or call at (520) 316-6960.

lakes.name: Pacific Avenue Athletic Complex Pond (PAAC)
lakes.description:
Surrounded by views of the Gila, Kofa and Castle Dome mountains, Pacific Avenue Athletic Complex (PAAC) Pond is Yuma's newest fishing destination. The City of Yuma partnered with the Arizona Game and Fish Department to stock PAAC Pond with a varity of sport fish, providing residents and visitors with fishing opportunties.

For more information on PAAC amenities and guidelines for visiting, visit Pacific Avenue Athletic Complex Pond, or call (928) 373-5243.

lakes.name: Painted Sky Park at Blossom Rock
lakes.description:
Painted Sky park features a 1.5- acre lake that offers catch and release fishing and walking paths, shared ramadas and open lawn space. Only single barbless hooks can be used. A valid fishing license is required for any angler over 10 years old.

This lake is located in Apache junction at 10109 S Dutchman Dr. Apache Junction, AZ 85120.

lakes.name: Paloma Park Lake
lakes.description: Paloma Park community fishing lake located within an 85 acre greater Paloma park system. This water follows the "lake" bag limits of the community fishing program

lakes.name: Papago Park
lakes.description: The Papago Park Ponds are made up of three separate ponds for a combined total of 6 acres. Pond 1 is 1 acre with a maximum depth of 8 feet. Pond 2 is 2 acres with a maximum depth of 7 feet. Pond 3 is 3 acres with a maximum depth of 11 feet. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. For additional information, please visit Phoenix Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (602) 256-3220.

lakes.name: Parker Canyon Lake
lakes.description:
Parker Canyon Lake is located 30 miles southwest of Sierra Vista in the Canelo Hills on the Coronado National Forest. Depending on the time of year, this 125-acre lake offers both coldwater and warmwater fishing, as well as a variety of other outdoor recreational activities. Parker Canyon Lake is popular with anglers from all over southern Arizona for its high quality bass fishing and winter stockings of rainbow trout. Catfish can be caught from shore, and a 5-mile trail around the lake provides opportunities to see wildlife, including Coues white-tailed deer, a small subspecies of white-tailed deer found in Arizona, New Mexico and Mexico.

There is a fish consumption advisory for largemouth bass and bluegill in Parker Canyon Lake. See ADEQ for more information.

lakes.name: Patagonia Lake
lakes.description:
Patagonia Lake is located 10 miles northeast of Nogales within Patagonia Lake State Park. In the late 1960s the Lake Patagonia Recreation Association built Patagonia Lake and the recreation facilities. Arizona State Parks purchased the lake and facilities in the mid 1970’s. Since then, Arizona State Parks and the Arizona Game and Fish Department manage the lake cooperatively.

Other amenities include a fishing pier, visitor center, and park store. There is a fish consumption advisory for flathead catfish in Patagonia Lake. See ADEQ for more information.

lakes.name: Patterson Ponds
lakes.description:
Patterson Ponds, located in the rural community of St. Johns in the White Mountains of northeast Arizona, became an Arizona Game and Fish Department-Community Fishing Program water in 2016. Kids and their families can easily ride their bikes to Patterson Ponds after school or on the weekends and spend a few hours fishing.

The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks the ponds at least two times per year with trout, three times per year with catfish, and once with sunfish.

Patterson Ponds include an upper pond (5-acre) and lower pond (3-acre) for a combined total of 8 acres, and is open 24 hours a day. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. For additional information, please visit St. Johns Parks and Recreation, or call at (928) 337-4517, ext. 221.

lakes.name: Perkins Tank
lakes.description: Perkins Tank is a 3.5 acre stock tank Located ~15 miles southeast of Williams, AZ, on the Kaibab National Forest. Amenities at the tank include a parking area, pit toilet, and walk-in access to the tank. The road into Perkins Tank may be closed due to snow. Perkins Tank usually has unsafe ice cover beginning in December through February.

lakes.name: Peña Blanca Lake
lakes.description:
Peña Blanca Lake was built in 1957 by the Arizona Game and Fish Department. Located 8 miles northwest of Nogales on the Coronado National Forest, this scenic 45-acre lake along the Mexican border is surrounded by rolling grasslands. At an elevation of 4,000 feet, Pena Blanca Lake has cooler temperatures than the surrounding lower elevation Sonoran desert. Facilities at this popular destination were renovated in 2009, including an improved boat launch and fishing pier. The lake is one of the stops along the historic Ruby Road scenic drive.

There is a fish consumption advisory for largemouth bass in Pena Blanca Lake. See ADEQ for more information.

lakes.name: Pioneer Lake
lakes.description: Pioneer Lake is a 5 acre lake with a maximum depth of 12 feet. The lake is located within Pioneer Community Park, and can be accessed between 6:00 a.m. and 10:30 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. Leashed dogs are permitted in the park. For additional information, please visit Peoria Community Services, or call at (623) 773-7137.

lakes.name: Rainbow Lake
lakes.description: By damming Walnut Creek in 1903, Mormon settlers created Rainbow Lake. Eventually, the settlement grew into the Town of Lakeside, now incorporated as the Town of Pinetop-Lakeside. Despite being surrounded by homes, Rainbow Lake remains open to the public for fishing, boating, bird watching, or just enjoying the outdoors.

lakes.name: Red Mountain Lake
lakes.description: Red Mountain Lake is an 8 acre lake with a maximum depth of 17 feet. The lake is located within Red Mountain Park, and can be accessed between sunrise and 10:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. No distilled alcoholic beverages permitted. Pets are not allowed in the park. For additional information, please visit Mesa Parks, Recreation and Commercial Facilities, or call at (480) 644-2352.

lakes.name: Redondo Lake
lakes.description: Redondo Lake is an 11 acre lake with a maximum depth of 14 feet. The lake can be accessed 24 hours a day. There are no facilities on site. For additional information, please contact the Arizona Game and Fish Department Yuma Regional Office at (928) 342-0091, or the Bureau of Reclamation Area Office at (928) 343-8100.

lakes.name: Riggs Flat Lake
lakes.description: Riggs Flat Lake, located 42-miles south of Safford, is a small, 11-acre scenic lake at the top of the Pinaleño Mountains in alpine forest and meadows. The Arizona Game and Fish Department built Riggs Flat Lake in 1957 to provide trout fishing opportunities in southern Arizona. A narrow, winding road leads to Riggs Flat Lake and campgrounds, weather permitting. The Coronado National Forest typically opens the road leading to the lake on April 15, and closes it on Nov. 14. Call the Coronado National Forest Safford Ranger District at (928) 428-4150 for the most up-to-date information, or go to Coronado National Forest - Riggs Flat Lake.

lakes.name: Rio Vista Pond
lakes.description: Rio Vista Pond is a 2.7 acre pond with a maximum depth of 14 feet. The pond is located within Rio Vista Community Park, and can be accessed between 6:00 a.m. and 10:30 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. Leashed dogs are permitted in the park. For additional information, please visit Peoria Community Services, or call at (623) 773-7137.

lakes.name: River Reservoir
lakes.description:
Originally built in 1896 on the Little Colorado River, River Reservoir is the largest and deepest of a trio of lakes collectively known as the Greer Lakes.

The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks this 50-acre lake with fingerling rainbow trout in the spring and 12" rainbow trout in the spring and summer. Like its two neighboring reservoirs, River Reservoir gets a few brown trout from the Little Colorado River diversion that refills it in the winter, but browns are not stocked here. Wild brown trout can get quite big in the lake. As it is an irrigation reservoir, the lake is drawn down considerably by late summer. Check the fishing report for fishing, water quality and boat accessibility.

lakes.name: Riverview Lake
lakes.description: Riverview Lake is a 3 acre lake with a maximum depth of 16 feet. The lake is located within Riverview Park, and can be accessed between sunrise and 10:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Pets are not allowed in the park. For additional information, please visit Mesa Parks, Recreation and Commercial Facilities, or call at (480) 644-2352.

lakes.name: Roadrunner Park Lake
lakes.description: Roadrunner Pond is a 2 acre pond with a maximum depth of 8 feet. The pond is located within Roadrunner Park and can be accessed between 5:30 a.m. and 11:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. An alcoholic beverage permit is required. For additional information, please visit Northeast Phoenix Division Parks and Recreation, or call at (602) 262-6696.

lakes.name: Roosevelt Lake
lakes.description:
A large, 20,300-acre reservoir on the Tonto National Forest, Roosevelt Lake generally has excellent fishing opportunities for largemouth bass and crappie that have been aided by Arizona Game and Fish Department's installation of fish habitat (see a map). The Arizona Game and Fish Department also has stocked thousands of Florida-strain largemouth bass that can reach sizes up to 20 pounds. Roosevelt has good camping opportunities and is situated near trout-stocked streams below the Mogollon Rim that make for extended days of fishing action.

Water levels fluctuate annually due to water releases by the Salt River Project to meet water demands. Check the daily water level report.

Roosevelt Lake Wildlife Area - posted portions closed to public entry from November 15th through February 15th annually.

There is a fish consumption advisory for channel catfish and largemouth bass in Roosevelt Lake. See ADEQ for more information.

lakes.name: Roper Lake
lakes.description: Roper Lake is located in Roper Lake State Park, approximately 6 miles south of Safford. The main part of the park was developed in the early 1960’s as a private recreation area. The Arizona Game and Fish Department acquired the 32-acre lake and surrounding lands in 1969, later transferring the property to Arizona State Parks. Roper Lake State Park has many amenities, including a fishing lake, swimming beach, picnic shelters and ramadas, day-use areas, campgrounds and cabins, and a store. More info, including park entry fees, can be found at Roper State Park.

lakes.name: Rose Canyon Lake
lakes.description:
A relatively small lake (7 acres), Rose Canyon Lake is nestled in mature ponderosa pines high on the slopes of the Santa Catalina Mountains. Just 30 miles (48 km) northeast of Tucson, anglers fish the lake all year long, though rainbow trout are stocked only April - October and brown trout in the fall. A paved road through Rose Canyon Campground leads to a small parking area, a short walk away from the water.

While Rose Canyon Campground closes October-April, the lake is still accessible by foot if you walk the road or park near the hiking trail. Call the Coronado National Forest Santa Catalina District at (520) 749-8700 for the most up-to-date information, or go to Coronado National Forest-Rose Canyon Lake.

lakes.name: Russel Tank
lakes.description: Russell Tank is a 4.5-acre pond on the Kaibab National Forest.

lakes.name: Saguaro Lake
lakes.description: Surrounded by towering formations of jagged rocks, and rows of saguaro cacti on the shorelines, the scenic recreation area of Saguaro Lake can be a bass angler’s paradise and generally harbors some of the biggest largemouth bass in the state. Over 2,200 fish habitat structures have been installed to enhance fishing. This popular, 1,264-acre reservoir on the Tonto National Forest, has opportunities for boat and slip rentals, as well as picnic and hiking opportunities.

lakes.name: Sahuarita Lake
lakes.description: Located an half an hour drive south of Tucson in Sahuarita, this 10-acre lake is located in Sahuarita Lake Park, which is open to the public sunrise to sunset. The 15-acre park has large grassy areas, with several picnic areas and benches along a 1-mile pathway. The Town of Sahuarita partners with the Arizona Game and Fish Department's Community Fishing Program to stock fish and host family fishing days several times a year. Public restrooms are located at the north and south ends of the lake. Swimming is not allowed in the lake. For additional information, please visit Sahuarita Parks and Recreation, or call at (520) 822-8896.

lakes.name: Santa Fe Reservoir
lakes.description: Santa Fe Reservoir is located south of the city of Williams, AZ on the 4th street/Perkinsville road. It is named after the Atchison, Topeka, and Santa Fe Railway, who built the Santa Fe Dam to hold water for use in its steam locomotives. This small reservoir is easily fished from shore or by small watercraft. However, launching a boat on a trailer is not advised.

lakes.name: Show Low Creek
lakes.description:
This section of Show Low Creek is the first creek to join the Community Fishing Program!

The 0.7 mile section of the creek opened for community fishing includes the reach beginning near the Hampton Inn and Suites and runs downstream to the foot bridge at the Show Low Bluff Trail.

Come out and catch rainbow trout in the winter and spring, or catfish and sunfish in the warmer months! Other park amenities include hiking trails and a Frisbee golf course.

lakes.name: Show Low Lake
lakes.description:
Attention walleye anglers...Show Low Lake is the best place in Arizona to catch lunker walleye!

Show Low Lake has yielded the last five state records, and numerous “Big Fish-of-the-Year Program” walleye catches. Local resident Gregg Munck caught the existing state record walleye here in November 2002. It weighed in at a whopping 16 lbs., 2 ozs. Anglers can also catch trout, catfish, bass and panfish here.

Show Low Lake has 100 surface acres with an average depth of 33 feet and maximum depth of 50 feet. It’s situated at an elevation of 6,500 feet. The lake maintains good water quality year round, and the Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks rainbow trout from April through September, and occasionally channel catfish. The lake also contains reproducing populations of walleye, largemouth and smallmouth bass, bluegill and green sunfish. Show Low Lake is open year-round.

lakes.name: Silverbell Lake
lakes.description: Silverbell Lake is a family-friendly 13-acre lake located in Tucson's Danny Lopez Park, and is open to the public 6:00am-10:30pm. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. No live baitfish allowed. No fishing is allowed in Archer Lake. For additional information, please visit Tucson Parks and Recreation, or call at (520) 791-4873.

lakes.name: Steele Indian School Park Pond
lakes.description: Steele Indian School Pond is a 2.5 acre pond with a maximum depth of 12 feet. The pond is located within Steele Indian School Park, and can be accessed between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. An alcoholic beverage permit is required. For additional information, please visit Phoenix Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (602) 495-0739.

lakes.name: Stone Dam Lake
lakes.description: Originally built by Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railroad in 1902 to store water for use in the railroad's steam locomotives, the 10-acre Stone Dam Lake is located between Williams and Ash Fork, AZ.

lakes.name: Sundance Park Lake
lakes.description: Sundance Lake is 3.2 acres in size with a maximum depth of 14 feet.

lakes.name: Surprise Lake
lakes.description: Surprise Park Lake is a 5 acre lake with a maximum depth of 12 feet. The lake is located within Surprise Community Park, and is open between sunrise and 10:00 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. For additional information, please visit Surprise Community Parks and Recreation Services, or call at (623) 222-2000.

lakes.name: Tempe Town Lake
lakes.description: Tempe Town Lake is a 224 acre lake with a maximum depth of 18 feet. Park hours are between 5:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. Anglers may fish from 5:00 a.m. until midnight. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. Alcoholic beverage permits are required. For additional information, please visit Tempe Parks and Recreation Department, or call at (480) 350-5200.

lakes.name: The Pond at Town Hall
lakes.description: This small pond is located at the Gilbert Civic center. The pond is catch and release only with a requirement to use single barbless hooks.

lakes.name: Topock Marsh
lakes.description:
Located on the Havasu National Wildlife Refuge, Topock Marsh is a shallow, 4,500-acre backwater of the Colorado River, and serves as a critical stopover area for migratory waterfowl. Refuge visitors enjoy many outdoor activities, including fishing, boating, kayaking, canoeing, and birdwatching.

Anglers have many places to fish on Havasu National Wildlife Refuge. See more information about fishing on the refuge, including hotspots and access points. A portion of Topock Marsh is closed during the waterfowl hunting season, from October 1 to the end of the season. Signs and buoys mark off closed areas.

lakes.name: Tunnel Reservoir
lakes.description:
The smallest of a trio of lakes on the Little Colorado River, Tunnel Reservoir provides just one of many trout fishing opportunities in and around the alpine town of Greer. The Greer Lakes, as they are collectively known, include Bunch, Tunnel and River Reservoirs, and are a short distance apart from each other. Each is accessed from FR 87B. Tunnel Reservoir is the first lake on the right, immediately after the turnoff on the left to Bunch Reservoir.

Tunnel Reservoir has an average depth of 10 feet. The 15-acre lake is filled in the winter through a diversion off the Little Colorado River. The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks catchable-sized rainbow trout in the spring and summer. Occasionally, a few brown trout make it into the lake from the diversion. As it is an irrigation reservoir, the lake is drawn down considerably by late summer. Check the Arizona Game and Fish Department fishing report for fishing, water quality and boat accessibility.

lakes.name: Upper Goldwater Lake
lakes.description:
Nestled in tall pines, beautiful Goldwater Lake is just four miles from downtown Prescott in Goldwater Park. This small, 15-acre lake is popular with outdoor enthusiasists and families looking to fish, or paddle a kayak or canoe. The park has several picnic areas, and a well-worn trail hugs the shoreline, offering many places to drop a line while enjoying spectacular views. The park has modern restroom facilities, ramadas, barbeque pits,and a fishing pier. For information on hours and parking fees, visit City of Prescott Goldwater Lake Park.

The Arizona Game and Fish Department recently began stocking Gila trout, a rare trout species found only in Arizona and New Mexico. For the first time in nearly 50 years, anglers have opportunities to fish for this threatened species, contributing to its recovery and conservation. In June 2018, a world record Gila trout was caught by an angler out of Goldwater Lake.

Canoe and kayak rentals are available from Prescott Outdoors.

lakes.name: Veterans Oasis Lake
lakes.description: Veterans Oasis Lake is a 5 acre lake with a maximum depth of 14 feet. The lake is located within Veterans Oasis Park and is accessible between 6:00 a.m. and 10:30 p.m. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. An alcoholic beverage permit is required. Fishing is prohibited in the recharge basins. Dogs must remain on leashes at all times, and are not permitted at the lake or recharge basins. For additional information, please visit The Environmental Education Center, or call at (480) 782-2890.

lakes.name: Water Ranch Lake
lakes.description: Water Ranch Lake is a 5 acre lake with a maximum depth of 15 feet. The lake is located within the Gilbert Riparian Preserve at Water Ranch, and can be accessed between 6:00 a.m. and 10:30 p.m. Bass and Sunfish may only be caught on a catch-and-release basis, and must be immediately released unharmed. Fishermen may only utilize single barbless hooks. Swimming, wading, glass containers, and littering are prohibited. No fishing is allowed from the bridge. For more information visit Gilbert Community Services, or call at (480) 503-6200.

lakes.name: Watson Lake
lakes.description: Located just 4 miles from downtown Prescott in the scenic Granite Dells, Watson Lake is framed by a unique collage of rising and falling boulders, making for a particularly surreal paddling and boating experience. A disc golf course and hiking trails coupled with excellent weather during the summer makes Watson an outdoor recreation destination the whole family can enjoy.

lakes.name: West Wetlands Pond
lakes.description:
The West Wetlands Pond is located in one of Yuma's favorite parks, West Wetlands Park, along the banks of the Colorado River in the Yuma Crossing National Heritage Area. The City of Yuma has partnered with the Arizona Game and Fish Department to stock the 1.3 acre pond with a varity of sport fish, providing residents and visitors with fishing opportunties year round. After you're done fishing, go play in the sand at Centennial Beach and build a sandcastle or two, then check out the Hummingbird and Butterfly Gardens. The park has also added burrowing owl habitat, so don't miss seeing these delightful creatures.

For more information on West Wetland Park, visit Yuma Parks and Recreation, or call at (928) 373-5200.

lakes.name: White Horse Lake
lakes.description: White Horse Lake is located on the Kaibab National Forest south of Parks, AZ. Whitehorse Lake is a popular camping, fishing, and paddle sports location. Amenities at the lake feature two campgrounds, pit toilets, paved roads and parking areas, day use area, boat launch, concessionaire, kayak and canoe rentals. Access to White Horse Lake is by the Parks exit off I-17, Garland Prairie road, Thomas Loop Road, FR141, and FR 109.

lakes.name: Willow Creek Reservoir (Willow Lake)
lakes.description:
Willow Lake is located just a few miles outside of downtown, and is popular for fishing and paddling sports such as kayaking and canoeing. A multiuse trail encircles the lake, and birdwatchers and wildlife lovers will enjoy viewing migrating waterfowl at Audubon Society's Watson and Willow Lakes Ecosystem Important Bird Area.

Stop by the Willow Lake Archaeological Interpretive Center for a self-guided tour with interpretive signage to view three excavated pithouses, circa 850 - 1100 A.D.

lakes.name: Willow Springs Lake
lakes.description:
Constructed by the Arizona Game and Fish Department in 1967, Willow Springs Lake is one of the largest and most popular lakes on the Mogollon Rim. Located on the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest at an elevation of 7,500 ft., this narrow, 158-acre reservoir offers excellent shoreline fishing. Fishing from boats is also very popular. The Arizona Game and Fish Department stocks trout in the lake weekly during summer months.

In addition to trout, Willow Springs Lake also has illegally stocked warmwater fish, including bass and green sunfish. The Arizona Game and Fish Department encourages anglers to catch and keep as many of these species as possible. The presence of these species makes it difficult for the Arizona Game and Fish Department to manage Willow Springs Lake as a quality trout fishery, and the presence of these warmwater species also threatens the existence of native fish species downstream.

lakes.name: Woodland Reservoir
lakes.description:
Located in the heart of Pinetop-Lakeside, Woodland Lake and the park surrounding it have been called the town’s “Crown Jewel.” In addition to trout fishing, the lake provides a host of other outdoor recreation opportunities, and is heavily used by residents and visitors alike.

Woodland Lake is situated at 6,893 feet. At full capacity, it has a surface area of 18 acres with a maximum depth of 20 feet.
